_comment: `klt power` base spec for ADC_BLOCK -- the IR-drop / electromigration
read issue #346 asks for, on the supply geometry issue #330's `klt erc`
run found: both rails are one electrical island each, with ZERO
Metal2-Metal5 area, stitched block-to-block through Poly2 risers.
klt power layout/adc-top/adc_block.gds \
layout/power/adc_block.power-spec.json --format json
Run bare like that, this spec is EXTRACTION-ONLY: it declares no `pads`
and no `current_model`, so `klt power` reports the resistive network and
leaves `ir_drop_map`/`worst_case_droop_mv`/`em_verdict` null. That is
deliberate -- where the supply is landed and what each sub-block draws
are not properties of this layout, they are assumptions, and they live
in `layout/power/cases.json` where each one is named, sourced and
asserted. `run_power.py` composes this file plus one case's assumptions
into the spec it actually runs, and commits that composed spec beside
the report.
LAYER NUMBERS -- the same ones, from the same two sources
Every (layer/datatype) pair below is identical to
`layout/erc/adc_block.supply-spec.json`'s, and was derived there from
the installed PDK's own layer table
($PDK_ROOT/gf180mcuD/libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp, open_pdks
c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b) cross-checked against
klayout-tools' curated gf180mcu deck. See that file's own _comment for
the derivation; it is not repeated here, because a second transcription
is a second chance to get it wrong.
The ONE structural difference from the ERC spec: `klt power` has no
`role`/`active_layer` concept (it has no gates to identify), so Poly2
is declared here as an ordinary conductor. That is the right model for
this question -- the Poly2 risers really do carry supply current -- and
it is why `stackup[0]` is Poly2 in both files for different reasons.
SHEET RESISTANCE -- where every number comes from
The values below are the gf180mcuD NOMINAL corner. The pessimistic and
optimistic corners live in `cases.json`'s `resistance_corners` and are
substituted into a copy of this file per case; nothing here is a
one-corner-only claim.
Primary source: the PDK's own Magic techfile,
$PDK_ROOT/gf180mcuD/libs.tech/magic/gf180mcuD.tech, section `# Layer
resistance`, whose own header states `Resistances are in milliohms per
square` and cites foundry document `180MCU_YI-141-EP059-01_10.pdf`. It
carries three `variants` blocks -- `()` nominal, `(hrhc),(hrlc)`
high-resistance, `(lrhc),(lrlc)` low-resistance:
role     techfile line            nominal   pessimistic  optimistic
Poly2    resist (allpolynonres)     7.3        15.0          1.0
Metal1   resist (allm1)/metal1      0.090      0.104         0.076
Metal2   resist (allm2)/metal2      0.090      0.104         0.076
Metal3   resist (allm3)/metal3      0.090      0.104         0.076
Metal4   resist (allm4)/metal4      0.090      0.104         0.076
Metal5   resist (allm5)/metal5      0.060      0.070         0.050
Contact  contact pc                 8.0        15.0          0.0
Via1-4   contact m2c/m3c/via3/via4  4.5        15.0          0.0
`allpolynonres` is the ROUTING-poly flavour: the techfile's separate
`rpp` (350 ohm/sq) and `rnp` (310 ohm/sq) lines are the drawn
poly-RESISTOR flavours, which is what `layout/adc-top/lib/geometry.py`
quotes and what the comparator's load resistors are made of. Those
bodies are carved out by `devices[]` below and are NOT this rail.
Conflating the two would overstate the riser resistance ~48x.
Independent cross-check, metal only: the standard-cell tech LEF
$PDK_ROOT/gf180mcuD/libs.ref/gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0/techlef/
gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__{nom,max,min}.tlef carries `RESISTANCE RPERSQ`
0.090 / 0.104 / 0.076 for Metal1-Metal4 -- the same three numbers, from
a different file written by a different tool flow. The LEF publishes no
RPERSQ for Poly2 (it is `TYPE MASTERSLICE` there, not a routing layer),
so the poly number has one source, not two, and that is stated rather
than papered over.
WHAT THIS CORRECTS. Issue #346's body says Poly2 sheet resistance is
`roughly three orders of magnitude above Metal1's`. It is not: 7.3 /
0.090 = 81x nominal, 15.0 / 0.104 = 144x at the pessimistic corner --
about TWO orders, not three. The claim was unsourced when filed (the
Curator flagged it as such) and the ~48x poly-resistor-vs-routing-poly
confusion above is the likely origin. The measured answer does not
depend on which is right; the record says so anyway, because the number
is now sourced and the old one should stop being quoted.
EM CURRENT-DENSITY LIMITS -- and the two roles that have none
Source: the same standard-cell tech LEF as above, whose `UNITS` block
declares `CURRENT MILLIAMPS 1`:
Metal1-Metal4  DCCURRENTDENSITY AVERAGE 0.67  -> 6.7e-4 A per um of
drawn width
Metal5         DCCURRENTDENSITY AVERAGE 1.5   -> 1.5e-3 A/um
Via1-Via4      DCCURRENTDENSITY AVERAGE 0.18  -> 1.8e-4 A per cut
Poly2 and CON (33/0, the Contact role) are declared in that LEF as
`TYPE MASTERSLICE` / `TYPE CUT` with NO current-density line at all, and
a grep of the whole installed PDK for DCCURRENTDENSITY/mA-per-um finds
nothing else. So no limit is declared for them here -- `klt power`
counts their edges `unchecked` rather than guessing, which is why this
block's EM verdict is `pass_partial` and not `pass`. The roles the
block-level rail actually runs through are exactly the two with no
published limit; see `layout/power/README.md` for what is reported
instead (the solved current density in A/um per Poly2 riser, derived
from the report itself).
A CAVEAT ON THE VIA LIMIT that the committed reports do not lean on but
a reader should know: 0.18 mA is a per-CUT figure, and `klt power`'s
model is one resistor per merged via polygon. An array drawn as one
merged shape would be compared against a single cut's limit -- a
conservative direction, but not a tight one. It does not bind here:
no Via1-Via4 edge is on either supply island at all (both rails are
Poly2 + Metal1 + Contact only), which is the finding this whole flow
exists to price.
DEVICES -- the same two bodies klt erc already declares
Identical in shape and intent to `layout/erc/adc_block.supply-spec.json`
's `devices[]` (klayout-tools#2183 for `klt erc`, #2260/#2271 for
`klt power`): the comparator's two poly load resistors on Poly2, and the
CDAC's MiM unit capacitors whose plate-to-plate bridge IS the Via4
role's own geometry in this stream. Without them a resistor body is
solved as wire and the droop is computed on a net that is not the rail.
`provenance`/`devices[].body_area_um2` in every committed report is the
cross-check that each declaration bit.
NETS
`vdd` and `vss`, matched by label text on Metal1_Label 34/10 -- the only
layer this block puts text on. Four `vdd` labels and four `vss` labels,
one pair each in ADC_DECODE_BANK_N, ADC_DECODE_BANK_P, ADC_TOP_SW and
COMPARATOR. VSUBS is again not declared, for the same reason the ERC
spec does not declare it: it carries no label text in this stream.
